content:
Back in mid-October, a tipster on Weibo said the iPhone 18 was scheduled to enter production at the end of November, and that it would launch in March alongside the iPhone 18e. Today the same tipster says that neither model has entered mass production yet, and that the start has been pushed back to around New Year's Day.
Interestingly, this time he points to late October as the original target, which doesn't quite match what he claimed last month. Anyway, January would be later than either of those.
Bloomberg's Mark Gurman recently said the iPhone 18e is expected in February or March, with the standard model arriving around the same time. If that schedule holds, a production start around New Year's Day would give Apple less time than usual to build stock.
So it's unclear if the company will delay the launch somewhat, or keep it on schedule - in the latter case we might see some shortages in the first few weeks of availability. Regardless of what will happen, we're sure to hear a lot more about all of it in the coming weeks, so stay tuned.
Source (in Chinese)
